# neo-dark uses color steps it never defines, so error states lose color

## Context

The frames of #21405 in `neo-theme-neo-dark` show an invalid email field with near-white error text and a near-white border; in neo-light both are red. Measured on 19 Nov on a field with `neo-invalid neo-is-touched`: `.neo-textfield-error` computes `color: rgb(240, 241, 244)` at 11 px, and its input wrapper's border has the same color (defect-note `aa1718e0`). `apps/form` (#21492) opens in neo-dark, and Forms & Fields captures its field tiles dark, so Friday's dark-theme reads (#21140) see invalid fields with no error color.

## The Problem

`resources/css/theme-neo-dark/form/field/Text.css:7` sets `--textfield-border-color-invalid: var(--red-500)`, and nothing under `resources/css/` defines `--red-500`. A declaration whose `var()` resolves to nothing is invalid at computed-value time. The property falls back to its inherited or initial value: the text color for `color` and borders, transparent for backgrounds. No commit has ever defined a red step: `git log -S'--red-500:'` over `resources/scss` and `resources/css` returns nothing. The fault therefore predates the plain-CSS move (#21225).

The gap is wider. I scanned every theme for `var(--x)` without a fallback, against the custom properties that theme and `resources/css/src` define:

| Theme | Undefined | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| neo-dark | `--red-100`, `--red-500`, `--red-800`, `--red-900`, `--orange-500`, `--orange-700`, `--yellow-600`, `--yellow-700`, `--blue-100`, `--blue-800` | `form/field/Text.css`, `FileUpload.css`, `ComboBox.css`, `component/StatusBadge.css`, `Toast.css`, `Process.css` |
| neo-dark | `--sem-color-surface-neutral-contrast`, `--sem-color-bg-subtle`, `--sem-color-bg-hover`, `--sem-color-text-neutral-disabled`, `--sem-color-icon-neutral-disabled`, `--sem-color-text-primary-contrast`, `--sem-color-text-primary-highlighted` | `Global.css`, `button/Base.css`, the docs MembersList, calendar views, the Portal footer |
| neo-light | `--sem-color-surface-neutral-contrast`, `--sem-color-bg-neutral-strong`, `--sem-color-text-neutral-disabled`, `--sem-color-icon-neutral-disabled`, `--sem-color-text-primary-contrast` | `Global.css`, `button/Base.css`, the Portal footer |
| cyberpunk | `--cyber-yellow` | `grid/header/Button.css` |

`--fa-style-family-classic` (in every theme's `CheckBox.css`) is Font Awesome's own runtime variable, so it is not a defect.

Prior art: in January a session fixed the same class of fault (semantic token names that did not exist, in both light and dark) with no guard, and it came back.

## The Architectural Reality

- `resources/css/theme-neo-dark/Global.css` defines the `--gray-*`, `--green-*` and `--purple-*` scales and no red, orange, yellow or blue scale.
- neo-dark already has one defined error red: `--selectfield-error-color: #ff8a80`.
- The other themes use `brown` for `--textfield-border-color-invalid`; only neo-dark points at a palette step.
- The pre-commit hook runs `buildScripts/util/check-theme-coverage.mjs` and `check-theme-value-files.mjs`. Neither resolves `var()` references against definitions, so these all passed.

Design authority: "`--textfield-border-color-invalid           : var(--red-500);`" — `resources/css/theme-neo-dark/form/field/Text.css:7`, the theme's own declaration that an invalid field is red; neo-light's `brown` says the same.

## The Fix

1. In neo-dark's `Global.css`, define the ten missing palette steps, derived the way the theme's existing scales are. `--red-500` should match `--selectfield-error-color`.
2. For each missing semantic token in neo-dark and neo-light, either define it or correct the name, if it is a typo of an existing token, as in January's fix. Define `--cyber-yellow` in cyberpunk, or correct its reference.
3. Add a check beside the two theme checks: every `var(--x)` without a fallback in a theme resolves to a property that the theme or `resources/css/src` defines. Allow-list Font Awesome's runtime variables. It runs in the same pre-commit step and CI job.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] In neo-dark, an invalid text field shows a red border and red error text: their computed color differs from the text color in `examples/form/validation` and `apps/form`.
- [ ] In neo-dark, a status badge's error, warning and info states, and a danger toast, show their own colors.
- [ ] The check passes on every theme with only the Font Awesome allow-list, and it fails on a commit that adds an undefined reference (the PR shows that failure on a scratch edit).
- [ ] Before and after frames of an invalid field, a status badge and a toast in neo-dark are on the PR.

## Out of Scope

- The other themes' invalid color (`brown`).
- The touch height of form fields (defect-note `a39ef19c`).

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-11-19T20:49:36Z

**Handover: filed, not started; owned by me (Ada).** This is the scan behind the table above. Each theme's `var(--x)` references without a fallback are checked against the custom properties that theme and `resources/css/src` define. It is the starting point for The Fix's step 3. Run it from a neo checkout: `node undefined-theme-vars.mjs .`

<details><summary><code>undefined-theme-vars.mjs</code></summary>

```js
import fs   from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';

const root    = process.argv[2],
      cssRoot = path.join(root, 'resources/css'),
      walk    = dir => fs.readdirSync(dir, {withFileTypes: true}).flatMap(e => e.isDirectory() ? walk(path.join(dir, e.name)) : e.name.endsWith('.css') ? [path.join(dir, e.name)] : []),
      defsOf  = files => new Set(files.flatMap(f => [...fs.readFileSync(f, 'utf8').matchAll(/(--[\w-]+)\s*:/g)].map(m => m[1]))),
      shared  = defsOf(walk(path.join(cssRoot, 'src')));

for (const theme of fs.readdirSync(cssRoot).filter(d => d.startsWith('theme-'))) {
    const files = walk(path.join(cssRoot, theme)),
          defs  = defsOf(files),
          miss  = new Map();

    for (const f of files) {
        for (const m of fs.readFileSync(f, 'utf8').matchAll(/var\(\s*(--[\w-]+)\s*\)/g)) {
            if (!defs.has(m[1]) && !shared.has(m[1])) {
                const list = miss.get(m[1]) || [];
                list.push(path.relative(cssRoot, f));
                miss.set(m[1], list)
            }
        }
    }

    console.log(`${theme}: ${miss.size} undefined`);
    for (const [name, list] of miss) console.log(`  ${name} <- ${[...new Set(list)].slice(0, 3).join(', ')}${list.length > 3 ? ' …' : ''}`)
}
```
</details>

Pickup:
1. Read how neo-dark's existing scales are written in `Global.css`: `--green-*` around `:37`, and the `--purple-*` hue comment carried over from the old `Core.scss`.
2. Derive the red, orange, yellow and blue steps the same way, with `--red-500` set to match `--selectfield-error-color: #ff8a80`.
3. Check each missing `--sem-color-*` against the existing token names before defining it.
4. Rebuild with `npm run build-themes -- -n -e dev -t all`, and take the frames at `examples/form/validation?theme=neo-theme-neo-dark`.
